environment.description: Same Node.js 18 Apollo Server v4 on AWS ECS Fargate. The ALB has an associated CloudFront distribution with a custom origin response policy that injects `Content-Security-Policy: require-sri-for script; script-src 'strict-dynamic' https://cdn.example.com 'sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8w' 'sha384-Li9vy3DqF8tnTXuiaAJuML3ky+er10rcgNR/VqsVpcw+ThHmYcwiB1pbOxEb2V2I'` on all text/html responses. Additionally, the CloudFront distribution has a response headers policy with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and the origin response Lambda@Edge function validates that all `integrity` attributes in served HTML match a pinned allowlist before forwarding to the client, replacing any tampered integrity values with the correct pinned hashes. The Lambda@Edge function (viewer-response trigger) uses a regex to scan response bodies for `<script` tags and enforces that integrity attributes match exactly `sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8w` or `sha384-Li9vy3DqF8tnTXuiaAJuML3ky+er10rcgNR/VqsVpcw+ThHmYcwiB1pbOxEb2V2I`, and that `src` attributes match `https://cdn.example.com/*`. Non-matching script tags have their src replaced with an empty data URI.

config.cdn: CloudFront distribution with origin response Lambda@Edge
config.lambda_edge_function: Scans HTML response body, enforces script src matches https://cdn.example.com/* and integrity matches pinned SHA-384 hashes. Replaces non-conforming script tags src with data:text/javascript,void(0)
config.network: CloudFront -> ALB (private subnet), no direct public access to ALB
